ai.description: This stout snake reaches 1 meter. It is grey or olive with irregular dark blotches and a white belly. Key features include a blunt, rounded head and specialized scales for gripping crabs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Fordonia leucobalia* is best distinguished by its small, beady eyes and a single pair of enlarged chin shields, which differ from the multiple pairs found in similar water snakes.
ai.habitat: The crab-eating snake inhabits intertidal mangrove forests and muddy estuarine creeks across the coastal regions of the Indian subcontinent, typically at sea level.
ai.behavior: The crab-eating snake exhibits a unique "looping" maneuver, coiling its body around prey to anchor itself while using its jaws to tear off and swallow crab limbs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Fordonia leucobalia* is viviparous, producing litters of 3–14 young. In India, breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Fordonia leucobalia* is found in the coastal mangrove forests and tidal estuaries of the Sundarbans in West Bengal and Odisha, occurring at near sea-level elevations.
